stemMd: An experimental treatment makes the inner mitochondrial membrane highly permeable to protons. Electron transport continues, but ATP production falls. Why?

options.label: A
options.textMd: ATP synthase normally works without an energy gradient.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The proton gradient dissipates without driving ATP synthase efficiently.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The genetic code changes in every ribosome.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Oxygen can no longer accept any electrons by definition.

options.label: E
options.textMd: All glycolytic enzymes have been removed.

explanationMd: The electron transport chain pumps protons across the inner membrane. ATP synthase captures the energy as protons return through it. A proton leak bypasses that coupling, dissipating the gradient and reducing ATP yield despite continued electron transport.

distractorRationale.c: The intervention concerns membrane permeability, not codon assignments.
distractorRationale.d: The premise says electron transport continues.
distractorRationale.e: The treatment is directed at the mitochondrial membrane.
distractorRationale.a: Its synthesis of ATP is powered by proton flow down the gradient.
